author: suzialeksander
body: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/annotations?goUsage=descendants&goUsageRelationships=is_a,part_of,occurs_in&goId=GO:1901342&taxonId=147367&taxonUsage=descendants @Antonialock I'm not sure where these UniProt annotations are from, could you look and let me know if i need to assign someone else? It seems like GO:0010087 phloem or xylem histogenesis might be the intended area for an alternative GO, exact synonym is vascular tissue histogenesis This is from a user email: > I would like to first thank everyone maintaining and updating the GO as it is most definitely not an easy task. > > I have a question related to taxon constraints and GO hierarchy. As part of my research that involved creating GO subsets for Viridiplantae, I used the taxon constraints file to collect any GO terms related to plant functions. However, I noticed something interesting. Using QuickGO (GOA), I can see that the GO term “regulation of vasculature development” (GO:1901342) has been assigned to genes in two rice species (and they have been UniProtKB reviewed). Looking at its taxon constraint, it has the "only in Vertebrata" label. However, as seen from the assignments, this term can apply to plant products as well. Not only that, but its ancestor term “vasculature development” (GO:0001944) has the same constraint, yet plants do also have a vascular system. > > Another interesting thing is that “vasculature development” (GO:0001944) has the ancestor term “circulatory system development” (GO:0072359), this in turn can be very confusing if it is agreed that the former term’s taxon constraints would include plants and therefore encase a broader range of taxa than its ancestor’s. Briefly, I am not sure about the order and constraints of these two terms as plants do have a vascular system but not a circulatory system. Would it be possible to investigate these terms please?
title: Plants annotated to Only in Taxon 7742 Vertebrata
